Picture this: you've just spent four hours hauling a heavy trolley around 18 holes. Meanwhile, your Tesla drove itself home. If a car can navigate an open road autonomously, why can't a golf trolley follow you around a course?

That single thought launched iXi - a Belgian startup that went on to raise €860,115 in pre-sales on Indiegogo for the world's first autonomous golf trolley, with a marketing strategy that returned nearly every euro they spent on ads.

From Late-Night Side Project to Full Product Company

iXi started the way a lot of great companies do: on a shoestring. The two founders - both engineers - worked full-time jobs by day and built their prototype at night, funded by a classic 3F round: Friends, Family, and Fools. The original plan was to retrofit autonomous technology onto existing trolleys. Then they looked at what was actually on the market: a motorized cart with a two-button remote. That's it.

A key investor pushed them further: "What you're doing needs to be bigger. Be more ambitious." So they scrapped the retrofit idea and decided to design and manufacture the entire product from scratch - a Tesla-inspired golf trolley with integrated autonomous technology. The right call, but a far more expensive one.

Enter Laetitia and the Business Side

About a year in, Laetitia Freysen heard the founders pitch at an entrepreneurship event. She saw the potential immediately - and the gap. "It was all engineers. All they could do was develop a product. But in a startup, that's not enough." They needed someone to handle marketing, finance, contracts, and IP all at once. Laetitia raised her hand, and the team finally had its missing piece.

Choosing To Crowdfund

iXi didn't launch on Indiegogo to generate revenue. They launched to prove there was a market. Building a full hardware product meant massive fixed costs, and investors had one question: "Is there actually demand for this?" Getting real people to put down real money is the purest form of market validation that exists.

"Crowdfunding is where you're completely naked. It's only when people put their money down that you know it's for real." - Laetitia Freysen, iXi

The Pre-Launch Strategy That Made Everything Work

As engineers, iXi loved data and hated uncertainty. The LaunchBoom framework gave them a way to minimize both. The strategy was built around a reservation funnel - before the Indiegogo campaign went live, Meta ads drove traffic to a pre-launch page where visitors could reserve a VIP spot.

The Framework

A Reservation Funnel Built Around Data

Before the campaign launched, Meta ads drove traffic to a pre-launch page where visitors reserved a VIP spot. The promise was simple:

  • First to know when we launch
  • First access to the best deals
  • Regular updates leading up to launch day

iXi campaign image (to add)

Meta Advertising

Ads That Paid for Themselves

When the reservation fee jumped from $1 to $50, conversion rates barely moved - people were still signing up at nearly the same rate, at 50× the price.

Over the pre-launch period, iXi collected ~€52,000 in deposits against ~€60,000 in ad spend. Net marketing cost: just €8,000.

The funnel also became a demand forecasting tool. "Everyone had a different opinion on when to launch - one month, six months. The answer was: no. We need this many VIP reservations first." With historical conversion data, the team could calculate exactly how many reservations they needed to hit their campaign goal - minimizing risk with math instead of gut feeling.

The $50 Reservation That Changed Everything

Raising the reservation fee from $1 to $50 was uncomfortable. "We thought, we're not money grabbers. Fifty euros is real money." But the counter-argument won: when your product costs €5,000, a $1 deposit attracts the curious. A $50 deposit attracts serious buyers - and the data is dramatically more reliable.

"Think about it like Tesla's approach. When they launch a new vehicle, they collect $200 reservations. The company that inspired iXi's product also inspired their go-to-market strategy."

Launch Day

After two and a half months of building their VIP list, iXi was ready. The emails went out. The Indiegogo page went live.

"The first two minutes were exhilarating. Every time you refresh the page, boom, boom, boom. These are real people. They really like what we do." - Laetitia Freysen, iXi
  • 125 units sold - over $200K in pre-sales
  • Between $500K and $600K raised
  • €836,000 total

Then reality kicked in. Messages flooded every channel - email, social, the campaign page. Credit cards failing. VIP emails missed. The team did what engineers do: categorized every complaint and got to work. Launch day is a rollercoaster. Prepare for both the exhilaration and the chaos.

Adding Fuel with Viral Video

One organic effort punched way above its weight. The team filmed a video with the president of the Belgian PGA Pro Association using the trolley on a course - mostly because Instagram needed content. It went viral. More than three million views. Watch time off the charts.

"We weren't good enough at putting all the tracking in place because we just thought we'd do a video for Instagram. But it was viral. When you find the right influencer, it can really help tap into your target market. It's very powerful." - Laetitia Freysen, iXi

The Numbers That Matter

The Numbers That Matter

Ad spend (pre-launch) ~€60,000
VIP deposits collected ~€52,000
Net marketing cost ~€8,000
Total Indiegogo revenue €836,000
Return on ad spend Nearly 15×

Worth noting: iXi didn't spend a single euro on ads during the live campaign. Every euro of revenue traces back to the pre-launch reservation funnel - a rare result that shows just how effective a well-built pre-launch can be.

Using Crowdfunding Results to Raise Investment Capital

Remember, the whole point wasn't revenue - it was validation. When iXi went to raise their next round, the Indiegogo results became the centerpiece of their pitch. Selling 125 units in 10 minutes is the kind of proof point that makes investors pay attention.

The team intentionally capped sales at 300 units to manage manufacturing risk, ultimately selling 281. For investors, constrained demand is actually more compelling than unlimited sales - it signals demand exceeds supply, which is exactly what you want to demonstrate.

Lessons for Founders Ready to Launch

Laetitia's advice comes down to one core belief: Data beats opinions. Every time.

"I think crowdfunding should almost be a compulsory step in the guidebook of entrepreneurs. Money aside, it validates if you're on the right track." - Laetitia Freysen, iXi

On the pre-launch reservation strategy: "It's obvious now that I've done it. Why would you do it any other way?"

Key Principles That Made iXi's Launch Work

  1. Define your goal before you start. Revenue or market validation? The answer shapes every decision.
  2. Build a reservation funnel before you launch. Don't go live until the numbers support your goal.
  3. Charge a meaningful reservation fee. For high-price products, a $50 deposit filters for serious buyers and gives far better data.
  4. Let data tell you when to launch. Don't pick an arbitrary date - wait until reservations support your campaign target.
  5. Cap your units to manage risk. You can always sell more later. Overcommitting when costs aren't locked in is dangerous.
  6. Invest in beautiful visuals. iXi's product renders performed consistently well across every ad.
  7. Don't underestimate organic content. One well-placed influencer video drove millions of views.
